title: Uptight (1968) · Cleveland Location Review

scope.statement: The supplied review covers all 682 indexed stills. These are selected images from the roughly 104-minute film, not every frame of the moving picture.
scope.method: The report states that all indexed images were inspected in sequential contact sheets, promising details were examined at available individual-image resolution, and findings were compared with historical records and photographs. This update imports those findings and retains the website’s original frame IDs and timestamps.
caveats: Most source images reviewed in the PDF are 480 × 270 pixels. Timestamps refer to the website’s version of the film.
A strong visual identification locates a landmark or setting; it does not establish an exact camera position.
Editing does not prove geographic continuity, that interiors belong to the preceding exterior, or that all industrial inserts share one plant.
Movable signs, mascots, police insignia and scene dressing are not fixed geographic landmarks.

Sources S01–S29 and their access date follow the supplied review; C01–C02 are supplementary map-placement references checked for this update. Historical address dates and unresolved gaps remain part of each finding.

summary: Madison Square Building at Hough Avenue / East 79th Street is a probable identification in frame 63, with the remaining facade-match gap stated explicitly.
Eagle Avenue Lift Bridge is a strong visual identification in frames 638 and 652.
The former West 3rd Street bridge hypothesis is replaced by an unpinned, probable former Clark Avenue Bridge candidate in frames 653, 654, 657 and 658.
East 86th Street / Wade Park Avenue is documented as a filming area in a contemporary account; no indexed still has yet been matched to that evidence.
The Save-Way directory evidence dates to 1974. Unresolved business and interior leads retain their uncertainty, while the Atlanta and Los Angeles sequences are distinguished from Cleveland.

confidenceDefinitions.label: Strong visual identification
confidenceDefinitions.description: A distinctive visual match supported by location evidence; no exact film camera coordinate is implied.

confidenceDefinitions.label: Strong contextual identification
confidenceDefinitions.description: A landmark’s form and position within an identified view agree with a historical comparison.

confidenceDefinitions.label: Probable
confidenceDefinitions.description: Converging clues support the candidate, with a material photographic, historical or geographic gap.

confidenceDefinitions.label: Unplaced
confidenceDefinitions.description: An inspected observation or research lead with no defensible shooting address assigned.

confidenceDefinitions.label: Documented filming area
confidenceDefinitions.description: A source records the production’s presence in an area, even though no individual indexed still has been matched.

geographicExclusions.name: Los Angeles nightlife sequence

locationRegister.name: Western Reserve Building / Superior Hill

locationRegister.name: Detroit–Superior Bridge

locationRegister.connection: The central steel arch appears in the river views; concrete approach arches and the former streetcar deck are especially clear in frames 642 and 644. The review supports frames 635–637 and 642–646. These views identify several Flats settings without proving a single continuous walk or drive.

locationRegister.name: Former Clark Avenue Bridge / steelworks area
locationRegister.address: Former Clark Avenue crossing in the industrial valley; exact film viewpoint unresolved
locationRegister.confidenceNote: Clark Avenue is a stronger candidate than the previous West 3rd Street attribution. The review does not provide an identical road-level historical view, so no replacement pin is asserted.
locationRegister.connection: Frames 653, 654, 657 and 658 show a road bridge beside blast-furnace equipment and a long, high-level through-truss with dense overhead bracing. The tall structure in frame 654 is furnace apparatus, not a lift-bridge tower. Bridge form and the industrial relationship make the former Clark Avenue Bridge the better candidate.
locationRegister.pinNote: Unpinned: the review explicitly calls for withdrawing the West 3rd Street pin without publishing an exact replacement location.

locationRegister.connection: The street-speech sequence in frames 151–169 includes Leader Drug. Frames 151 and 153 add a red FURNITURE KRO… sign, plausibly Kronheim. A branch directory plus matching frontage or neighboring business is still needed.

locationRegister.name: Steelworks / ore yards — unplaced
locationRegister.address: Industrial-valley lead; plant and parcel unknown
locationRegister.confidenceNote: The ore piles, bucket gantry and industrial apparatus do not establish a steel company, plant parcel or a common shooting site for all industrial inserts.

locationRegister.name: Madison Square Building / Hough Avenue
locationRegister.confidenceNote: The MADISON roof lettering, corner blocks, balconies and drugstore cornice converge with the address record, a 1964 corner photograph and a 1972 aerial. The archive photograph does not show the full central arch and balcony pattern, so the identification remains probable.
locationRegister.connection: Frame 63 shows a long brick apartment/commercial building with heavy white corner blocks, stacked balconies and a tall central arch. MADISON is readable on the roof; SQUARE is less legible. The historical corner comparison supports the inference without conclusively matching the full facade. Frames 58–62 may belong to the local sequence, but their properties remain unassigned.
locationRegister.pinNote: Approximate Hough Avenue / East 79th Street vicinity; this pin does not establish the demolished building footprint or camera position.
